newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch clear up "hidden" copper stocks mystery.
newsitem.headline: Dutch clear up "hidden" copper stocks mystery.

text.p: The Dutch Statistical Office (CBS) on Wednesday admitted it had supplied flawed data on flows of copper through Rotterdam, clearing up a puzzle over "missing" stocks of the metal which threw world markets into disarray.
CBS import and export figures supplied to the World Bureau of Metal Statistics last month seemed to indicate over 500,000 tonnes of hidden copper was lying in Rotterdam warehouses.
A WBMS report drew this conclusion after comparing the Dutch figures against official London Metal Exchange (LME) data.
The report was largely rejected by traders and analysts but the theory, coming in the wake of the Sumitomo trading scandal, still rattled the market and sent world copper prices tumbling.
The CBS told Reuters on Wednesday the inaccuracies in its data completely explained how the WBMS had drawn its conclusion.
"The amounts fully match up," a spokesman for the CBS said. "This accounts for the copper."

The WBMS report was based on data covering a period between 1990 and 1995 and concluded that the discrepancy could have been caused by hidden copper, although it suggested other scenarios involving Russian shipments and "statistical anomalies".
"If we look at the numbers around 600,000 tonnes of copper appears to have gone into warehouses and not come out," Lloyd Davies, WBMS General Manager, said at the time.
The CBS said its own three-week investigation into the data seemed to solve the puzzle of the missing copper.
The main reason for the problem, it said, was a failure to distinguish between copper imported into the Netherlands for domestic use and copper passing through the country in transit.

In the period between 1990 and 1993, flows of copper through the port were not fully included in official statistics and after 1993 some copper registered as being for use within the Netherlands had found its way onto the wider European Union market, the report said.
